strategy.thesis: TELUS is a Canadian telecommunications company whose strategic investment arm, TELUS Global Ventures (formerly TELUS Ventures), treats health tech as a core pillar alongside IoT, AI and security, on the premise that 'corporate Canada should take a greater interest in the country's healthcare'; it invests in digital health, precision medicine and diagnostics startups that complement TELUS's own TELUS Health business line.

sources.title: TELUS Ventures announces new equity investments in Canadian Precision Medicine and Diagnostics companies
sources.supports: existence, sector focus on precision medicine/diagnostics

sources.title: Rich Osborn on how TELUS Ventures is transforming Canada's medical landscape, one investment at a time
sources.supports: founded 2001, deal pace (6-10/yr), avg check size $4-5M, ~30 company active portfolio, health as core pillar
sources.quote: TELUS Ventures makes six to 10 deals a year – each with an average investment of $4 million to $5 million – and currently manages an active portfolio of nearly 30 companies.

sources.title: Clinia secures Series A funding, partnership with Telus Health to deploy its health search tech
sources.supports: Clinia investment, TELUS Ventures led $10M CAD Series A

verification_notes: Brand was renamed from 'TELUS Ventures' to 'TELUS Global Ventures' in recent years per current telus.com URLs; both names used interchangeably in press. Portfolio count and check size figures are for the fund overall (health + IoT/AI/security), not health-only.

strategy.thesis: Wittington Ventures is the venture investment platform of Wittington Investments, the holding company for the Weston family group that owns grocery/retail giant Loblaw, Shoppers Drug Mart and Choice Properties; it invests in tech companies across consumer, commerce, healthcare and climate, giving Loblaw's non-medical retail/food empire a formal window into digital-health and health-AI startups.

sources.title: About - Wittington Ventures
sources.supports: investment focus, $500M platform size, backing from Wittington Investments/Weston group
sources.quote: We invest in tech-focused companies that affect the daily lives of millions across consumer, commerce, healthcare, and climate sectors.

sources.title: What Wittington Ventures' investments reveal about the future of Loblaw
sources.supports: founded 2019, 17-company portfolio as of April 2026, notable health investments (Abridge, WellBeam, Doctronic, Grey Matter Neurosciences)

verification_notes: A related name 'Wittington Innovation Fund' also appears in press coverage of the Grey Matter Neurosciences deal; treated here as the same platform/family pending clarification. Loblaw itself (via Shoppers Drug Mart/PC Health) has made separate direct strategic investments (e.g. Maple Corp) that are not confirmed to route through Wittington Ventures specifically.

check_size.raw: $25M-$150M per transaction, up to hundreds of millions via LP co-investment

strategy.thesis: Sagard Healthcare Partners is the dedicated healthcare royalty/credit strategy of Sagard, the alternative-asset management platform founded by Power Corporation of Canada (a diversified financial-services and insurance holding company); it provides non-dilutive royalty and credit financing to owners of IP behind approved, commercialized biopharmaceutical products, diagnostics and medical devices, giving a non-medical financial conglomerate dedicated healthcare exposure.

people.name: David MacNaughtan
people.background: 25-year biopharmaceutical industry veteran; previously ran the intellectual-property investment strategy at Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB)

strategy.thesis: Co-operators, a Canadian insurance and financial-services co-operative, runs a Corporate Venture Capital fund that backs early-stage Canadian tech companies aligned with its insurance/financial-services mission; its highest-profile health-related bet is BlueDot, the infectious-disease-surveillance startup that identified the COVID-19 outbreak from Hubei province before it was widely reported.

sources.title: Corporate Venture Capital fund
sources.supports: fund purpose, BlueDot investment and COVID-19 detection claim
sources.quote: Co-operators was a lead investor in BlueDot, a health-tech company using data analytics to track infectious disease spread. In early 2020, BlueDot gained international recognition by identifying COVID-19 in Hubei province before widespread awareness.

verification_notes: Fund is a generalist insurtech/fintech-leaning corporate VC (contact is 'VP Corporate Development'); health is not its primary sector focus, but BlueDot is a clearly documented, notable health-tech investment. Only one primary source found this session.

strategy.thesis: GreenShield Ventures is the venture studio and innovation hub of GreenShield, Canada's only national non-profit health-and-benefits insurer; it incubates, acquires and invests in digital-health, mental-health and benefits-administration startups that are embedded into the GreenShield+ integrated payer platform, giving an insurance-sector parent (rather than a pharma/medtech company) a dedicated health-venture arm.

sources.supports: identity as venture studio/innovation hub of GreenShield
sources.quote: GreenShield Ventures serves as the venture studio and innovation hub of GreenShield, Canada's only national non-profit health care and insurance organization.
